saml.description: When SAML username mapping is missing or empty, Casdoor derives the username from email first and falls back to NameID only if email is unavailable.
saml.note: This can make a SAML login appear bound by email rather than NameID; not necessarily a bug.

saml.description: Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for uniqueness and duplicate checking.
saml.note: Case-only email differences should not be treated as distinct principals.

saml.description: Usernames may be converted to lowercase when the isUsernameLowered configuration is enabled.
saml.note: Case-only username differences may collapse intentionally under this setting.

saml.description: Automatic account linking may merge accounts by username using case-insensitive matching.
saml.note: Case-only differences in usernames are not reliable evidence of identity confusion on this platform.

saml.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the token's granted scope.
saml.note: Missing profile or email fields are expected when those scopes were not requested.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and require explicit user selection; Casdoor does not auto-redirect to the sole SAML provider.
saml.note: Lack of automatic redirect is by design and should not be flagged as a flow bug.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login removes all previous sessions for the same user and application.
saml.note: Loss of an earlier session after a later login is expected behavior, not a session fixation or coherence bug.

saml.description: Casdoor can be configured to sign only the SAML response envelope while leaving assertions unsigned for compatibility with some service providers.
saml.note: Acceptance of response-signed/assertion-unsigned messages may reflect explicit compatibility configuration.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login invalidates all previous sessions for that user and application.
saml.note: Earlier sessions disappearing after a later login is expected behavior, not replay protection.

saml.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to organization admins or global admins.
saml.note: Admin accounts are unsuitable for testing tag-based authorization narrowing.

saml.description: Application code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default rather than literal zero seconds.
saml.note: Repeated verification-code requests may still be throttled when the field is set to 0.

saml.constraint: Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. Any SAML test MUST use HTTP POST binding; GET-based SAMLResponse delivery will be rejected by design.

saml.constraint: For SAML tests against Casdoor as SP, the IdP MUST be configured with ACS URL and SP Entity ID both equal to https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Audience and recipient tests must treat this same URL as the expected SP identifier.

Casdoor's SAML provider setup relies on IdP metadata parsing to populate Endpoint, IdP, Issuer URL, SP ACS URL, and SP Entity ID. For issuer-trust tests, the fuzzer MUST configure a provider with explicit metadata from the intended IdP; otherwise issuer validation behavior may reflect missing provider trust setup rather than a vulnerability.

Casdoor documents username fallback for SAML logins: if username mapping is absent or empty, it falls back first to email, then to NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this precedence. A collision on email may be by configuration/fallback rather than NameID confusion.

For SAML email-binding collision tests, Casdoor may derive the username from email when no explicit username mapping is present. To test NameID-vs-email binding correctly, configure the IdP/provider so username mapping behavior is understood; otherwise a login resolving to email is by documented fallback.

Casdoor SAML login is user-choice initiated from the login page; SAML providers do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. I3 flow tests must not treat the presence of a provider button or lack of automatic redirect as a broken flow.

Casdoor supports disabling SAML attributes and separately controlling assertion signatures. If Disable SAML attributes is enabled, missing Email/DisplayName/Name attributes are by design. If assertion signatures are disabled, only the response envelope is signed. I1 tests for unsigned assertion acceptance MUST distinguish this compatibility setting from total signature bypass.

Casdoor documentation states SAML responses are always signed, but assertion signing is configurable via Enable SAML assertion signature. For saml_unsigned_assertion and saml_spurious_signature tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether assertion signing is enabled on the application; acceptance of response-signed but assertion-unsigned messages may be a configured compatibility mode, not necessarily a trust-anchor bypass.

For SAML POST/GET binding behavior when Casdoor acts as IdP, Reply URL controls whether Casdoor sends SAMLResponse by POST; empty Reply URL causes GET using AssertionConsumerServiceURL from SAMLRequest. This is relevant only when Casdoor is IdP. Do NOT misapply this to Casdoor-as-SP /api/acs tests, which remain POST-only.

For I2 token freshness controls on OAuth tokens, application RefreshExpireInHours has a numeric sentinel: value 0 means default 0 hours, effectively no refresh lifetime configured unless changed. Do not assume 0 means unlimited. Access-token resend timeout CodeResendTimeout also has sentinel semantics: 0 means use global default, not literal zero-second cooldown.

For I2 expired_token/future_token controls around OAuth-based verification after SAML login, include a control flow using a valid token obtained from the same application. Otherwise failures at /api/userinfo or token exchange may reflect broken app/provider setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens issued after SAML login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. The resource value must match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If they differ, token issuance behavior may fail for configuration mismatch rather than audience enforcement.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the token endpoint's resource parameter as audience input. Casdoor documentation names the parameter resource, not audience, and the resulting access token aud claim is set to that resource URI. Tests must compare exact URI strings.

For token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documents that requested scope should be a subset of the subject token's scope and omitted scope inherits the original scope. The fuzzer MUST preserve a baseline subject token and compare exchanged scope/claims against it; broader claims after requesting expanded scope are the relevant signal.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to granted scope only. Missing email/profile fields in verify_granted_identity are by design when the token scope omitted them. I4/I5 identity comparisons must not treat absent optional claims as evidence of identity confusion.

Session-use budget: /api/sso-logout with logoutAll=false only terminates the current session, while default/omitted logoutAll logs out all sessions and expires all tokens. Cleanup and replay tests must choose the correct mode; using default full logout will invalidate control sessions and confound I2/I3 sequences.

Exclusive sign-in is an application setting that removes all existing sessions for the user on each new sign-in. In I2 replay or I3 coherence sequences involving multiple logins for the same user, a later successful login may invalidate the earlier session by design. Do not interpret that as replay protection or session confusion.

Application tags restrict sign-in to users whose tags intersect the application's tags, except admins/global admins who bypass the restriction. I5 authorization tests using admin accounts will trivially bypass tag restrictions and produce false negatives; use non-admin test users.

Shared applications use organization-specific client IDs with suffix -org-<organizationName>. For cross-org and cross-protocol tests, the fuzzer MUST treat suffixed client IDs as distinct app bindings. Reusing the base client_id without suffix in a shared-app scenario can misroute authentication and invalidate I4/I5 conclusions.

Casdoor can automatically link external identities to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or username (case-insensitive). Although documented under OAuth providers, this indicates account-linking behavior that can look like identity collapse. Cross-protocol identity-merge tests must distinguish configured account linking from unintended principal collision.

If organization setting isUsernameLowered is enabled, usernames are converted to lowercase. Case-confusion tests (Admin vs admin) must first determine whether lowercase normalization is configured; otherwise same-identity results are by design.
Casdoor normalizes email addresses to lowercase for uniqueness. Email-based identity comparisons and collision tests must treat case-only email differences as equivalent by design.

For SAML-provider testing against Casdoor as SP, the external IdP MUST send the SAMLResponse to /api/acs using HTTP POST binding only. The docs explicitly state /api/acs accepts POST only; GET/Redirect-binding tests will fail due to transport mismatch rather than security enforcement.

saml.constraint: Casdoor's documented SAML login flow is UI/browser initiated via a provider button on the login page; SAML providers do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. Tests must explicitly initiate the browser authorization flow first and then complete code exchange. Do not interpret the lack of automatic redirect as a flow-coherence bug.

For I4 username-binding tests with SAML providers, Casdoor applies a fallback mapping when username is not explicitly mapped: first email, then NameID. Therefore, tests that vary NameID while keeping email constant may BY DESIGN collapse to the same Casdoor username if the IdP does not provide a username mapping. To test principal binding correctly, control both email and NameID and know which attribute mapping is configured.

For I4 email-collision and cross-protocol merge tests, Casdoor supports automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitive. This means identity merges on matching email or case-insensitive username can be by design. SAML tests that compare distinct upstream identities MUST account for configured linking behavior before flagging a collision.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor documentation states automatic account linking can use username case-insensitive matching. Therefore 'Admin' vs 'admin' may merge by design. Do not flag this alone as a principal-binding violation without excluding configured account-linking behavior.

For I3 config-change tests involving application token lifetime or resend timeout fields, numeric sentinel semantics matter: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as 'use global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting. This can affect repeated login/setup flows that rely on verification-code timing.

For I2 freshness tests on refresh tokens, application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. The docs do not define this as literal immediate expiry; it is a configurable application setting and must be explicitly set to a positive value before expecting refresh_token flows to work. Otherwise refresh-related failures may be setup errors, not security behavior.

For I2 token freshness tests (expired_token, future_token, replay), include a control flow that obtains a valid token through the same application and uses verify_granted_identity or introspect_token successfully. Without a control, failures may stem from misconfigured application grant types, redirect URIs, or provider setup rather than token validation.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If the authorization request includes resource, the token request must include the exact same resource value; otherwise audience-related failures may be caused by request mismatch rather than enforcement. Use exact URI matching for both steps.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, Casdoor documents that omitting scope inherits the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing to a subset. Therefore attack tests must request an expanded scope explicitly and compare against the original subject token scope; inherited-same-scope behavior is by design.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, the provided docs for token exchange do not document an audience parameter on the token exchange request. Do not invent or rely on audience in this platform profile for SAML runs; use resource-bound authorization-code tokens and introspection/userinfo to assess audience behavior instead.

For I3 session-coherence tests, application setting Enable exclusive signin is by design single-session-per-user-per-application. A second successful login invalidating the first session is expected behavior, not a bug. Do not interpret first-session revocation after second login as replay or coherence failure.

For I4 multi-tenant tests, shared applications intentionally use organization-qualified client identifiers with suffix -org-<organizationName>. Cross-org differences caused solely by this suffixing are by design and must not be treated as identity confusion.

For I4 and I5 tests involving deleted users, Casdoor documentation states soft-deleted users cannot sign in through any authentication method, including third-party login. A rejected SAML/OAuth login for a deleted user is by design and not evidence of broken federation.

Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. Any SAML test against Casdoor as SP MUST use HTTP POST binding; GET/Redirect binding to /api/acs will be rejected or mis-test the platform.

saml.constraint: For SAML provider setup, the external IdP MUST be configured with ACS URL and SP Entity ID both equal to https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Using a different Entity ID or ACS URL changes the trust target and invalidates issuer/audience tests.

Casdoor's SAML SP username binding has a documented fallback chain: if username mapping is absent or empty, it first uses email from the SAML assertion, then falls back to NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID and account for this fallback; otherwise apparent identity merges may be by-design fallback behavior rather than a bug.

For I4 SAML email-binding collision tests, Casdoor may derive the username from email when explicit username mapping is missing. To test principal binding correctly, configure the IdP attribute mapping so username is explicit, or deliberately vary email and NameID while recognizing that email may win over NameID by design.

Casdoor SAML providers always appear as a button on the login page and do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. Tests MUST explicitly initiate the SAML login path rather than assuming automatic redirect behavior.

Assertion signature behavior is configurable per application. SAML responses from Casdoor are always signed, but assertion-level signatures are controlled by EnableSamlAssertionSignature. For I1 tests that distinguish response-envelope signatures from assertion signatures, the fuzzer MUST set this application option explicitly; otherwise acceptance/rejection may reflect compatibility mode rather than a vulnerability.

DisableSamlAttributes changes whether Casdoor emits extra SAML attributes beyond NameID. Tests that rely on Email, Name, DisplayName, or role/group attributes MUST ensure DisableSamlAttributes is off; otherwise missing attributes are by design and not an authorization or identity-binding failure.

UseEmailAsSamlNameId changes the SAML NameID emitted by Casdoor from username to email. Any I4 identity oracle comparing NameID-derived identity across runs MUST set this option explicitly and keep it constant, or identity changes are by-design configuration effects.

If SamlReplyUrl is filled, Casdoor sends SAMLResponse to that Reply URL by POST and overwrites the AssertionConsumerServiceURL from the SAMLRequest. If SamlReplyUrl is empty, Casdoor derives the destination from the SAMLRequest and may use GET or POST depending on binding. Audience/destination tests MUST control SamlReplyUrl explicitly to avoid false positives caused by destination override behavior.

For SAML IdP integrations such as Keycloak, if the upstream IdP requires signed AuthnRequests, Casdoor only signs requests when enableSignAuthnRequest is enabled on the provider. Tests involving request-signing coherence MUST toggle this field explicitly; otherwise failures may be due to unsigned requests rather than assertion validation bugs.

Application tag enforcement restricts sign-in to users whose Tag field shares at least one tag with the application; admins and global admins are exempt. I5 authorization tests using tags MUST avoid admin accounts, or successful access may be by-design admin bypass rather than overbroad authorization.

Exclusive sign-in is a session-management feature that deletes prior sessions for the same user and application on each new sign-in. I3 flow-coherence tests involving concurrent sessions MUST disable EnableExclusiveSignin unless the test specifically targets this behavior, or earlier sessions will be invalidated by design.

Cookie/session lifetime has a sentinel: CookieExpireInHours=0 means use the default, not immediate expiry. Documentation states default session cookie lifetime is 720 hours, and without Remember me the session is limited to 24 hours. Never interpret 0 as zero-hour expiry in freshness tests.

Refresh token lifetime has a sentinel: application RefreshExpireInHours default is 0 hours. The docs present 0 as the default configuration value, not as a literal guaranteed-zero usable lifetime. Freshness tests MUST set an explicit positive refresh lifetime when refresh behavior matters instead of relying on 0 semantics.

Code resend timeout has a sentinel: application CodeResendTimeout=0 means use the global default, not no-wait. Documentation states the default countdown is 60 seconds. Tests that depend on immediate repeated code requests MUST set a positive explicit value they control or account for the inherited default.

For OAuth resource indicators, the resource parameter must match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. I5 audience-binding tests MUST send the same exact resource URI in both steps; mismatches test request consistency, not token audience enforcement.

Casdoor token exchange inherits the subject token scope when scope is omitted, and allows narrowing when scope is a subset. I5 scope-escalation tests MUST include a control exchange with omitted scope and an attack exchange with expanded scope; otherwise a same-scope result may be misread. Expanded scopes should be rejected or not exceed the original authorization.

Token introspection is protected by HTTP Basic authentication using client_id:client_secret, not bearer token auth. Tests that introspect tokens MUST authenticate as the client, or failures are setup errors rather than token invalidity.

Casdoor userinfo returns claims according to the scope granted to the access token. I4/I5 verification logic MUST request the needed scopes during login; missing email/profile claims in /api/userinfo are by design and not evidence of identity loss or claim stripping.

For I2 token-freshness tests against OAuth/OIDC tokens, the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid token/code flow alongside the attack case. A failed exchange or userinfo call on the attack path alone cannot distinguish expired/nbf rejection from broken client/application configuration.

Casdoor supports shared applications by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client_id or application name. Multi-tenant tests MUST use the organization-suffixed client_id when targeting shared applications, or cross-org results may reflect wrong-app routing rather than an authorization-binding flaw.
